span.label: Content and style are not fully independent, so the separation is only partial.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as limitations[0] - the separation is partial, and the paper says so in its own framing
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: No image satisfies both the content and the style constraint perfectly; a trade-off has to be tuned per image pair.
span.note: what this limits: every output image: THERE USUALLY DOES NOT EXIST AN IMAGE THAT PERFECTLY MATCHES BOTH CONSTRAINTS AT THE SAME TIME, so the result is a trade-off tuned per image pair
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: What the paper calls style is a texture statistic that discards the composition of the image, in a feature space built for something else.
span.note: what this limits: any reading of this system's style as a style in the art-historical sense: it is computed in a feature space originally designed to capture texture information, and the resulting representation captures texture but not the global arrangement of the image
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The headline separability claim is demonstrated in the objective function, which is where the two terms are separated.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that content and style are separable: what is shown is that the minimised loss function contains two well-separated terms for content and style, which is a property of the objective the authors wrote
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Which image you get is set by a balance the user picks for each pair of sources.
span.note: what this limits: any output shown here as a result of the method: for a specific pair of source images the trade-off between content and style is adjusted by hand to create visually appealing images
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The use for perception research is projected, not carried out.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that this method is a tool for studying visual perception: the authors envision it being useful for such studies, from psychophysics to neural recordings, rather than reporting one
